story.head: Who drives the play: the Senators
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Flyers (5-10-6) lost 3-2 in overtime to Edmonton on Nov 11, while the Senators (12-6-2) beat Colorado 4-3 in overtime on Nov 12. Going in, the Flyers are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Sens fourth in the Atlantic (tenth).
The Flyers’ record (.381) is about what their chances are worth. The Senators’ record (.650) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.573), largely because they’re 6-2 in one-goal games.

The Flyers block a lot of shots (4th), but get a lot of their shots blocked (31st). Philadelphia has scored 2.24 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. On the other side, the Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one. Beyond that, the Flyers roll four lines, but the Senators lean on their top six.

Matvei Michkov (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 21 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 21 GP) is next in line. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven goals in eleven games against Philadelphia since 2023-24. Drake Batherson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 20 GP) is next in line.

Samuel Ersson (3-3-2 / .884 SV% in 7 GS) will likely start for Ottawa. Philadelphia has two options in net: Dan Vladař (3-4-4 / .879 SV% in 11 GS) and Joseph Woll (2-6-2 / .901 SV% in 10 GS). Vladař has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 11. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Travis Green likes to send Amadio, Giroux and Greig out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Foerster, Zegras and Konecny. Elsewhere, the Senators usually control more of the chances than the Flyers do.

Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Mammoth are missing more right now.
